request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This window continues the subcontracting demo. It shows how work in progress items are transferred to a subcontractor with a transfer order and a new WIP ledger entry, and how item charges can be assigned to subcontracting receipts. It then covers the subcontractor pricing logic (closest match instead of best price, plus a minimum amount per line). The last part shows warehouse handling with warehouse receipts and inventory put-away, including serial numbers entered at any level. The presenter closes with a recap of what was shown. No status labels such as preview or GA are given, apart from a note that one warehouse scenario already existed in 28.3.

chapters.title: Attachments flow and the transfer WIP item on the routing
Transfer order to subcontractor and WIP ledger entry
Receipt, item charge assignment and cost recap
Warehouse receipt with serial numbers (directed put-away)
Inventory put-away on a basic location and wrap-up

features.name: Subcontracting attachments flow to production order and purchase
features.description: Attachments on the routing have toggles to flow to the production order and to the purchase document. The subcontracting description document was copied to the subcontracting purchase order.
prerequisites: Attachment on the routing with the flow toggles enabled

features.name: Transfer WIP item and WIP ledger entry
features.description: A routing line can be marked with a transfer WIP item, so work in progress goods are sent to a subcontractor for a later operation. Posting the transfer does not create item ledger entries for that line but registers a new work in progress ledger entry.
caveats: Makes little sense for the first operation, since nothing is work in progress yet
prerequisites: WIP item defined on the routing line
Subcontracting is not the first operation

features.name: Create transfer order to subcontractor
features.description: A subcontracting action on the production order creates a transfer order from the main location to the subcontractor location. It has one line for the component and one line for the transfer WIP item.
prerequisites: Production BOM component set to be transferred from own location

features.name: Subcontracting details fact box with WIP quantity
features.description: A fact box on the production order routing shows the WIP quantity at the subcontractor and allows drill-down to the WIP ledger entries. This shows how much must be transferred back, and fact boxes and actions link purchase, transfer and production orders.

features.name: Item charge assignment to subcontracting receipt lines
features.description: Item charges can be assigned to posted purchase receipt lines of a subcontracting order, including the operation line. The production order statistics then show the charge in actual subcontractor cost.
caveats: Actual cost only shows the item charges because the vendor invoice was not posted in the demo
prerequisites: Purchase invoice with an item charge line

features.name: Subcontractor prices with closest match
features.description: Subcontractor prices are matched by closest match on quantity, date, task, unit of measure and variant, not by the lowest price as in normal purchase pricing. A larger order can therefore get a higher unit price if the vendor price list says so.
caveats: Differs from standard purchase price logic, which picks the best price
prerequisites: Subcontractor prices defined on the item

features.name: Standard task codes
features.description: Standard task codes are now included in Dynamics 365 to make it easier to demonstrate different subcontractor pricing. They were not used in the demo.

features.name: Minimum amount per line for subcontractor price
features.description: If the line amount is below the vendor minimum amount, the price becomes the minimum amount divided by the quantity. In the demo, a minimum of 100 and quantity 2 gives a unit price of 50.
prerequisites: Minimum amount set on the subcontractor price

features.name: Subcontracting with warehouse receipt and item tracking (directed put-away)
features.description: For a white location with directed put-away, a subcontracting order needs a warehouse receipt. Serial numbers can be assigned and put-away created only when it is the last operation, otherwise the receipt registers the production output. The speaker says this was already in minor release 28.3.
features.status_evidence_quote: that's not something like very, very new because we already had it in minor release 28.3.
caveats: Serial numbers and put-away only for the last operation
prerequisites: Location with directed put-away and pick (white location)

features.name: Subcontracting with inventory put-away on a basic location
features.description: On a location that requires put-away and pick but has no warehouse receipt or shipment, the subcontracting order can be received through an inventory put-away. Serial numbers can be assigned there and quantity to handle can be auto filled.
caveats: Presenter wishes the convenient assign function also existed on this page
prerequisites: Location requiring put-away and pick without warehouse receipt or shipment

features.name: Serial numbers defined at any level in subcontracting
features.description: Serial numbers can be defined on the production order and copied to the purchase order, or defined on the purchase document and used to populate the inventory put-away. Any receiving method works: purchase document, warehouse receipt or inventory put-away.
caveats: Lot numbers were not demoed, the speaker says they work the same
